title: Tax Planning vs. Tax Evasion in Nepal: Understanding the Legal Difference
metaDescription: Learn the legal difference between lawful tax planning and illegal tax evasion under Nepal's Income Tax Act 2058. Protect your business from criminal penalties.
h1: Tax Planning vs Tax Evasion: Understanding the Difference
directAnswer: The fundamental difference is legality and transparency: tax planning uses legitimate statutory deductions, depreciation schedules, and tax incentives codified within the Income Tax Act 2058 to structure commercial affairs efficiently; tax evasion involves deliberate deceit, suppression of sales, falsified invoices, or unrecorded cash transactions, which constitutes a criminal offense under Section 120 carrying severe financial penalties and imprisonment.
author: Lalitpur Advisory Research Desk

sections.h2: Lawful Tax Planning vs. Illegal Tax Evasion
sections.contentHtml:
Understanding the statutory boundary protects business owners from severe regulatory action by the Inland Revenue Department (IRD) and Revenue Investigation Department (RID):

Lawful Tax Planning (Encouraged)

  • Optimizing statutory depreciation rates under Schedule 2 of Income Tax Act 2058.
  • Claiming eligible CSR expenditure deductions up to statutory caps.
  • Utilizing concessional 20% tax rates for qualified manufacturing entities.
  • Ensuring staff retirement contributions utilize CIT and SSF tax-exempt allowances.

Illegal Tax Evasion (Criminal)

  • Operating unrecorded sales counters or personal QR payment accounts.
  • Under-invoicing goods at customs borders or in domestic billing.
  • Purchasing fake VAT invoices (Fictitious Bills) to inflate expenses.
  • Maintaining double ledgers (Kachhi Khata vs Pakki Khata).

sections.h2: Severe Penalties Under Section 120 & RID Directives
sections.contentHtml: Section 120 of the Income Tax Act 2058 imposes a 100% fine on concealed tax, plus statutory interest, compounded with potential criminal prosecution by the Revenue Investigation Department (Rajaswa Anusandhan Bibhag). faqs.question: Can tax planning reduce our corporate tax legitimately?
faqs.answer: Yes. Proper structuring of capital expenditures, utilizing accelerated depreciation, claiming allowable staff welfare benefits, and structuring compliant inter-company charges significantly lowers effective tax burdens lawfully.
